parts.label: R
parts.ask: How much energy does an inductor store?

explain.say: A car's ignition coil turns a 12 volt battery into a spark of thousands of volts, and the secret is energy stored in a magnetic field. On the board, a battery drives current through a coil of 500 turns wound on an iron core, in series with a 6 ohm resistor. How much energy is hiding in that coil?

parts.label: R
parts.ask: How much energy does an inductor store?

explain.say: First, inductance. Current in the coil makes magnetic flux, and every turn links that flux. Inductance, L, is the flux linkage per amp: N times Phi, over I, measured in henries. A coil with high inductance builds a lot of field for each amp, so it fights changes in current strongly. Would more turns raise or lower L?

parts.label: R
parts.ask: How much energy does an inductor store?

explain.say: Raise it, by the square of the turns, because more turns make more flux and each turn also links it. For a long coil, L equals mu nought times N squared times the area, over the length. With 500 turns, 1 square centimetre and 10 centimetres long, an air core gives just 0.314 millihenries. An iron core with relative permeability 1000 makes it 0.314 henries. What does relative permeability measure?

parts.label: R
parts.ask: How much energy does an inductor store?

explain.say: How much more easily a material carries magnetic flux than empty space. Now the energy. Building up the current means pushing against the coil's back voltage, and that work is stored in its field: E equals half L I squared. At 2 amps, half of 0.314 times 4 is about 0.63 joules. See the curve bend upwards? What happens to the energy if the current doubles?

curves.label: E = ½LI², L = 0.314 H
curves.ask: How much energy does an inductor store?

explain.say: It quadruples, to about 2.5 joules at 4 amps. And where does the energy live? In the magnetic field itself, with an energy density of B squared over 2 mu nought. Open the switch suddenly and the coil dumps that energy in a flash, which is how an ignition coil makes its spark. Great work! Challenge: what inductance stores 1 joule at 1 amp?

faq.a: Inductance is the magnetic flux linkage a coil produces per amp of current, L equals N Phi over I, measured in henries. It measures how strongly a coil opposes changes in current.

faq.q: How do I calculate the inductance of a solenoid?
faq.a: L equals mu r times mu nought times N squared times the cross-section area, divided by the length. Doubling the turns makes L four times bigger.

faq.q: How much energy does an inductor store?
faq.a: Half L I squared, held in its magnetic field. A 0.314 henry coil carrying 2 amps stores about 0.63 joules.
asks: Energy stored in an inductor formula

faq.q: Why does an iron core increase inductance?
faq.a: Iron carries magnetic flux hundreds or thousands of times more easily than air, so the same current makes far more flux. That factor is the relative permeability.

faq.q: Where is the energy of an inductor stored?
faq.a: In the magnetic field inside and around the coil, with an energy density of B squared over 2 mu nought joules per cubic metre.

facts: A one henry inductor carrying one amp stores half a joule of energy.
The inductance of a coil grows with the square of its number of turns.
